videos.title: OpenAI Dumped Microsoft for Amazon — The $38B AWS Deal Explained
videos.description: OpenAI just ended its 7-year exclusive deal with Microsoft — and Amazon moved on it within 24 hours.  For years, if you wanted to build with GPT, you had exactly one option: Microsoft Azure. That exclusivity is now gone. Within 24 hours of the announcement, Amazon Web Services confirmed that GPT-5.5 and GPT-5.4 are now live on AWS Bedrock — the biggest shift in AI infrastructure since ChatGPT launched.  In this video, I break down exactly what happened, why it matters, and who wins and loses in this seismic power shift.  🕐 TIMESTAMPS: 0:00 - The shock announcement 0:15 - Why the Microsoft lock-in existed 1:00 - The $38B AWS deal explained 2:30 - What changed in the Microsoft-OpenAI contract 3:45 - What this means for developers 4:30 - Winners and losers breakdown 5:15 - My take: is this good or bad for AI? 7:15 - Subscribe & your thoughts  Here's what changed: Microsoft no longer holds exclusive cloud rights to OpenAI's models. They retain non-exclusive access through 2032, and OpenAI continues capped payments to Microsoft through 2030. But OpenAI is now free to license its technology to any cloud provider. And Amazon moved on this instantly — GPT-5.5 is now on Bedrock alongside Anthropic's Claude.  For developers, this is genuinely great news. Competition between Azure and AWS for AI workloads means better pricing, better performance, and no more forced multi-cloud setups just to access GPT. For Microsoft, it's a real blow — they just lost the moat that made Azure uniquely valuable to AI builders.  If you find this kind of AI analysis useful, subscribe — we cover every major shift the moment it breaks. videos.title: How to Adopt AI Agents in Your Enterprise with Google Cloud's Riyaz Habibbhai
videos.description: Live from Google Cloud Next 2026 in Las Vegas, Sam Charrington sits down with Riyaz Habibbhai, Director of AI Product Marketing at Google Cloud, to unpack the biggest AI announcements from the event.  The conversation focuses heavily on the shift from developer-centric tools to true enterprise-grade AI agents. Riyaz breaks down the launch of the Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform, explaining how Google is prioritizing "glass box" observability, governance, and seamless integrations using the Model Context Protocol (MCP). They also discuss the tangible business value of Google's "full stack" AI architecture—from TPUs to the application layer—and share real-world success stories, including how Macy's built a fully orchestrated voice agent in just four weeks.  If your organization is trying to navigate the transition from AI hype to secure, scalable agentic workflows, this episode of the TWIML Briefing Room is for you!  🔔 Subscribe to TWIML AI Podcast for more deep dives into Machine Learning and AI: https://twimlai.com/  ⏱️ Chapters:  00:00 - Introduction: Live from Google Cloud Next 00:30 - Key Themes: The AI-Optimized Stack & Interoperability 02:35 - Why a "Full Stack" AI Approach Matters to Customers 04:40 - The Evolution of Vertex AI into the Gemini Enterprise Platform 07:00 - Bridging the Gap Between Developers and Knowledge Workers 08:30 - "Glass Box" Observability & Agent Governance (Evals, Traces, & IDs) 10:23 - Breaking Down Enterprise Silos with a Unified Platform 13:23 - Embracing Openness: The Role of MCP (Model Context Protocol) 16:01 - Real-World Agent Adoption & Customer Success (Macy’s Case Study) 18:40 - Advice for Enterprises: Start with a POC & Build the Business Case 19:23 - Conclusion  🔗 Links:  Check out the TWIML Blog for more analysis: https://twimlai.com/articles Learn more about Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform: https://cloud.google.com/blog/products/ai-machine-learning/introducing-gemini-enterprise-agent-platform Follow Sam Charrington on LinkedIn: https://www.linkedin.com/in/samcharrington/ Follow Riyaz Habibbhai on LinkedIn: https://www.linkedin.com/in/riyaz/
